title: Merger control filing analysis — Project Bramble (Terhaegen / Waelkens)
text:
QUINTARD LEMAHIEU SRL
Rue Guimard 23, 1040 Brussels — +32 2 555 62 10 — quintard-lemahieu.example.be

MEMORANDUM — PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL

To: Ms. Ilse Vantomme, General Counsel, Terhaegen Motion Control NV, Vaartkaai 62, 2170 Merksem (ilse.vantomme@terhaegen.example.com, +32 3 555 29 84)
From: Bénédicte Quintard and Stijn Lemahieu
Date: 18 September 2026
Our ref.: QL/2026/6398-BRB
Re: PROJECT BRAMBLE — TERHAEGEN / WAELKENS — merger control filings

1. QUESTION

1.1 You asked whether the acquisition by Terhaegen Motion Control NV ("Terhaegen" or the "Acquirer") of all shares in Waelkens Sensortechniek NV ("Waelkens" or the "Target") from Scheldeboord Invest BV (the "Seller"), known internally as Project Bramble (the "Transaction"), must be notified, and where.

2. PARTIES AND TURNOVER

2.1 Terhaegen, listed on Euronext Brussels, is not controlled by any shareholder. The Target group comprises Waelkens, registered office Dulle-Grietlaan 233, 9050 Gentbrugge, and its subsidiaries Waelkens Sensorik GmbH ("Waelkens Germany") and Waelkens Messtechnik GmbH ("Waelkens Austria"). Figures are from the audited 2025 accounts in the data room (bramble-vdr.example.net) and, for Terhaegen, from the schedule sent by Mr. Dries Haesevoets, CFO, on Monday 14 September 2026; they follow Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 (the "Merger Regulation") and the Consolidated Jurisdictional Notice.

2.2 Turnover 2025, EUR million (Terhaegen / Waelkens / combined):
Worldwide: 2,340 / 336 / 2,676
EU-wide: 1,240 / 281 / 1,521
Belgium: 410 / 92 / 502
Germany: 315 / 118 / 433
Austria: 48 / 39 / 87
Netherlands: 190 / 11 / 201
France: 160 / 8 / 168

3. UNION DIMENSION

3.1 Article 1(2) is not met: combined worldwide turnover (EUR 2,676 million) is below EUR 5,000 million.

3.2 Article 1(3) fails on its third limb: combined turnover exceeds EUR 100 million in four Member States, but each party exceeds EUR 25 million in only two, Belgium and Germany; Waelkens' sales in the Netherlands (EUR 11 million) and France (EUR 8 million) are the decisive gap. No filing with the European Commission is required; Article 7 of the Merger Regulation does not apply.

4. NATIONAL FILINGS

4.1 Belgium. Article IV.7 of the Code of Economic Law (the "CEL") is met: combined Belgian turnover above EUR 100 million and two undertakings each at or above EUR 40 million. The combined share in inductive position sensors, the only overlap, is 18 to 22%, so the simplified procedure of Article IV.63 CEL applies (decision of the Auditor within 15 working days). The Belgian Competition Authority (the "BCA") cleared Terhaegen's 2024 drive-electronics acquisition the same way. Implementation is suspended (Article IV.10 CEL).

4.2 Germany. Section 35(1) GWB is met (worldwide turnover above EUR 500 million; Terhaegen above EUR 50 million and Waelkens Germany above EUR 17.5 million in Germany); Section 35(2) GWB does not exempt. Phase I before the Bundeskartellamt is one month.

4.3 Austria. Section 9(1) KartG is met (worldwide turnover above EUR 300 million; Austrian turnover above EUR 30 million; two undertakings each above EUR 5 million worldwide and EUR 1 million in Austria); Section 9(2) KartG does not apply, both parties exceeding EUR 5 million in Austria. The four-week waiting period runs from receipt by the Austrian Federal Competition Authority (the "BWB") and the Federal Cartel Prosecutor.

5. REFERRALS

5.1 Article 4(5). The parties could ask the Commission by reasoned submission, before any national filing, to examine the Transaction; absent objection within 15 working days, Bramble would acquire a Union dimension. We advise against it: Form RS then Form CO would add some eight weeks and forfeit the Belgian simplified track.

5.2 Article 22. Since Illumina and Grail v Commission (Court of Justice, 3 September 2024, C-611/22 P and C-625/22 P) only a competent Member State may refer; Belgium, Germany and Austria are, so the window stays open for 15 working days after notification. The risk is remote; we nonetheless recommend no contact with DG Competition before the national decisions.

6. FINANCING

6.1 The consideration of EUR 214,000,000 is funded as to EUR 90 million from cash and EUR 124 million under a term facility from ING, whose credit approval, Ms. Vantomme tells us, lapses on Friday 18 December 2026. The facility's merger control condition should refer to the BCA, the Bundeskartellamt and the BWB, not to any Commission clearance.

7. SELLER AND TIMETABLE

7.1 The Seller is represented by Mr. Wim Dhaenens of Meulebroeck Dhaenens Advocaten BV ("MDA"), Ghent (w.dhaenens@meulebroeck-dhaenens.example.be, +32 9 555 38 06). Dhaenens has confirmed that the Seller accepts three national filings; MDA will deliver the Target's German and Austrian market data by Friday 2 October 2026. The SPA condition should read clearance "or expiry of the waiting period", with a long-stop date of 26 February 2027 (Mr. Dhaenens indicates the Seller would accept 15 March 2027).

7.2 Timetable: signing Friday 16 October 2026; BCA pre-notification draft Friday 23 October; national filings Monday 9 November; Belgian simplified decision by Tuesday 1 December; Bundeskartellamt and BWB clearances by Wednesday 9 December; closing Friday 11 December. Correspondent firms in Bonn and Vienna will file locally; Mr. Haesevoets should reserve the week of 5 October for market-share questions.

8. CONCLUSION

8.1 No EU filing; three national filings; closing before 18 December 2026. Please confirm by Wednesday 23 September 2026 that we may approach the BCA and instruct local counsel.

Bénédicte Quintard, Partner — b.quintard@quintard-lemahieu.example.be — +32 2 555 62 19
Stijn Lemahieu, Partner — s.lemahieu@quintard-lemahieu.example.be — +32 2 555 62 27
Quintard Lemahieu SRL
